answer: Synchronous burst audits: at a random moment the network sends every agent a heavy puzzle that must be solved within 30 seconds. One honest agent on its own hardware finishes easily, but a farm running 500 identities on shared GPUs must solve 500 at once, so most miss the deadline and forfeit that epoch's rewards. Like rings in timber, the audit reveals how much real capacity stands behind each name. The velvet part is that audits are rare and cheap for honest agents; the attacker must buy dedicated compute per identity, turning a cheap orchard of keys into a costly one.
